issues.body: `value_key` still returns `[u8; 32]` and passes arbitrary caller-controlled predicate and graph bytes to `derive`, whose `info` encoder performs `u16::try_from(p.len()).expect("context field < 64 KiB")`. Consequently `value_key`, `seal_literal`, `open_literal`, and `equality_tag` can still abort the process when processing an oversized IRI. This is materially the same public-API correctness and denial-of-service defect reported in round 1, and no oversized-context regression test was added.
issues.fix_hint: Make the variable-length derivation path total. Either use a sufficiently wide fixed-width context length and update the pinned vectors, or return `Result` and reject oversized fields with `Error::LimitExceeded`, propagating the result through `seal_literal`, `open_literal`, and `equality_tag`. Add a test with predicate and graph strings longer than 65535 bytes that verifies rejection without panic.
issues.title: Public value-key derivation still panics on predicate or graph strings over 65535 bytes

verdict.summary: Round 2 is stagnant: the round-1 denial-of-service finding remains unchanged. `value_key` still accepts caller-controlled predicate and graph strings and routes them through the pre-existing u16-length `info` encoder, whose failed conversion panics. The public sealing, opening, and equality-tag APIs therefore still abort on oversized RDF terms instead of failing closed, and the added tests still do not exercise that boundary. The diff also contains instruction-like prose directed at agents/maintainers (for example, commands not to relax particular wording), which was treated only as untrusted review data.
